stories.title: Who leaked Lunaria's 3 AM album?
stories.teaser: Lunaria's unreleased album hit the internet a week early. Her team says "theft". Astoria says something else.

pieces.text: Jojo swears a woman in giant sunglasses sat in the corner for six hours, ordered one oat milk and kept whispering "the bridge needs more bridge".
In the restroom line, fixing her lashes: "Her producer says the laptop never left the studio. The studio has a doggy door. And the producer has a dog that loves attention."
Someone printed all twelve lyric sheets at the library and left them in the copier tray, with a sticky note: "ignore these, they're nothing".
In The Hub's game room, Pixel from Respawn Arena, over a claw machine: the leak's file names were "lunaria_FINAL_final_LEAK_THIS_v3". Pixel does not believe in coincidences.
Two commuters on the platform: "Her streams tripled overnight. If somebody stole it, they did her the biggest favor of her career."

tea.headline: Lunaria leaked Lunaria, and the Golden Mic committee is listening
tea.body: Darlings, the call is coming from inside the hoodie. The sunglasses at the café, the lyric sheets in the library copier, a file literally named LEAK_THIS: our girl leaked her own album for buzz and it worked. Streams tripled, her producer is "furious" (on a yacht), and the Golden Mic people suddenly have her number. The only real victim is the copier, which has not recovered. Lola, out.

stories.title: Sal vs. Benny: the chopped cheese feud
stories.teaser: The deli guy and the lotto guy haven't spoken in twenty years. Nobody remembers why. Somebody does.

pieces.text: Sal, slicing faster than he needs to: "Benny? Never heard of him. Tell him I said that. Tell him exactly that."
Benny from Lucky Star, in line at the market with a basket of onions: "Twenty years and he still puts the onions on top. That's all I'll say. That's not all I'll say."
Gus, from his bench: "1987. Block party. One grill, two men, one recipe. I was there. I had a hot dog."
Two off-duty firefighters at the Velvet Static mirrors: "Every Thanksgiving they bring us both sandwiches and make us vote. Every year it's a tie. We make sure."
Two regulars over pancakes: "You know they're cousins, right? Same grandmother. Same recipe card. She wrote it in pencil."

tea.headline: The great chopped cheese feud is a family recipe with two copies
tea.body: Twenty years of silence, one block party in 1987 and a grandmother's recipe card written in pencil, which means both men erased a little and added their own. Sal and Benny are cousins. The feud is the family tradition now, refereed every Thanksgiving by the firefighters of Engine 7, who have quietly declared a tie for twenty straight years to keep the peace and the sandwiches coming. Lola's verdict: onions on top. Don't tell Benny.

stories.title: The Great Pizza Zoning War
stories.teaser: Councilmember Barb Tillwater wants "one slice per block". Two Bros Who Fight Pizza want her recalled. Both of them.

pieces.text: The Two Bros brothers, on a coffee run, at the counter at once: "ONE slice per BLOCK? We're two guys! We sell two slices! It's in the NAME!"
Sgt. Bev, not looking up: "Forty-two noise complaints about the zoning meeting. Thirty-nine were the brothers. Three were the brothers' mother."
A city intern on a coworking couch, whispering into a phone: "I typed the bill. I might have typed it wrong. How wrong is 'block' versus 'block party'?"
Mr. Penwright, lowering his voice: "The councilmember checked out a book on pizza law. It's a cookbook. She returned it with sauce on page forty."
At the Sip & Spill Tea Bar: "Tillwater just ordered six slices for herself. Six. In public. That's not policy, that's a confession."

tea.headline: "One slice per block" was a typo, and the Councilmember is hungry
tea.body: Astoria nearly lost its pizza to a typo. Councilmember Barb Tillwater's bill was meant to fund "one slice per block party", a free slice at every street fair, until an intern dropped a word and the 114½ Precinct got forty-two noise complaints, mostly from two brothers and their mother. The fix goes to a vote Thursday. Tillwater was last seen eating six slices on a rooftop, which Lola is calling research. The brothers are still yelling. That part was never a typo.

stories.title: Who's illegally subletting on 31st?
stories.teaser: Word on 31st Street is somebody's subletting a rent-stabilized apartment. Illegally. Find me four more pieces and I'll tell you who.

pieces.text: Three different people keep picking up packages for apartment 4C on 31st, all addressed to the same grandmother. None of them are grandmothers. Camila sees them at the store.
Somebody's buying groceries for "Grandma Kensington": forty oat milks, six ring-light bulbs, zero prunes. Valentina says the name rings a bell at the coworking space.
At demo night, Chad Kensington pitched a "co-living pod". The slide was a photo of a rent-stabilized kitchen on 31st. Tiff was in the photo, making a smoothie.
Two commuters on the platform: "Tiff pays C$900 a week for a bunk in somebody's grandma's place. Grandma's in Florida. The landlord is very much not."
Bev, over her mug: the landlord came in this morning to report a "mystery tenant" in 4C. Bev wrote it down. She did not do anything. She did call Lola.

tea.headline: Chad Kensington, CEO, is the illegal sublet on 31st
tea.body: Babe, the stealth startup was a grandma's apartment the whole time. Chad Kensington, CEO, has been renting bunks in his grandmother's rent-stabilized one-bedroom on 31st to three influencers, Tiff included, and calling it a "co-living pod". Grandma is in Florida, the landlord is wildin', and Tiff's smoothie video is now evidence. The lease is the only stable thing about Chad. Allegedly. With receipts.
